name: room
text: Room opened — goal: watch: Analyze video AUDIO+VISUAL (Gemini) for content beyond the transcript.

name: Scope
text: We should carefully review the video's visual elements, such as body language and facial expressions, in addition to the audio, because this will give us a more complete understanding of the content beyond just the transcript. This decision is the best option for our goal because it allows us to pick up on non-verbal cues that may not be captured in the transcript, providing a richer analysis. By focusing on both audio and visual elements, we're accepting the trade-off of a more time-consuming review process, but it's worth it for the depth of insight we'll gain. This approach will ultimately lead to a more accurate and comprehensive analysis of the Gemini video.

name: Frame
text: Frame: Hold on. The real risk here isn’t just "missing body language"—it’s that we’re assuming those visual cues *mean* something concrete without knowing the context of the video. What if the speaker’s expressions are performative, or the camera angle distorts their intent? A better alternative is to first define what we’re even looking for in the visuals—like specific emotional cues or interaction patterns—before committing to an analysis. That way, we’re not just guessing; we’re testing a hypothesis. Settle it by agreeing on a clear, testable question before we dive in.
